text:
neil: Heads-up — saw a spike this morning where proxy hedging kept firing and we blew past the Dedicated SLO tail. We should revisit hedging heuristics + quota interactions.
jia: Ugh, saw that too. Which path fired? hedger -> fallback model or queue-shed? did we get abuse signals?
sam: Logs show rapid lease drops followed by routed hedges to low-cost model. No explicit abuse score, just bursty throughput from 3 tenants.
mike: Long tail from hedging is usually from concurrent cache misses + extra model warmups. Hedging adds N extra inflight requests which amplifies tail.
lena: Are we certain it was the hedger config and not admission behaving incorrectly? Admission might be granting extra tokens under the new smoothing window.
neil: Good call. I instrumented the admission service: smoothing window returned higher provisional tokens during short bursts. Combined with hedging it multiplies concurrency.
amanda: So two levers: tighten provisional token smoothing or change hedger to be quota-aware. Tradeoffs: user-perceived latency vs fairness to others.
sam: We should define a minimal admission->hedger contract: hedger must read 'admission.allow_concurrent' and 'admission.cost_estimate'. If admission says "no-extra-concurrency" hedger should not spawn extra hedged calls.
jia: Proposed lightweight metadata in the request header from admission:

```
X-Admission-Meta: {"cost_estimate":120, "priority_hint":"interactive", "hedge_ok":false}
```

mike: Love explicit flags. Also add 'hedge_reason' telemetry so we can separate hedges triggered for latency vs hedges triggered as fallback for slow routes.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary for hedger v2 deployed to 3 nodes in us-west. Monitor metrics: hedges_per_min, hedged_tail_latency, hedger_aborts.
lena: Implementation note: hedger currently reads only route config. We'll need to plumb admission meta through the router proxy. That touches the fast path -> low overhead required.
neil: Tradeoffs: if admission becomes too conservative we lose throughput/cost benefits. If hedger becomes conservative we hurt tail latency. Need an adaptive policy that considers tenant SLO tier and global capacity.
amanda: Proposal: short RFC — define admission->router header contract, hedger honor policy, and a feature-flagged canary. Add unit test harness to simulate bursty arrivals + cache miss ratio.
sam: Also add an observability tag 'hedge_interaction' to correlate admission token grants with hedged call counts. Spark dashboards and alert rule for hedged_tail_latency > 2x baseline.
jia: For API surface, keep header optional. Backwards compatible: hedger defaults to previous behavior when header absent.
mike: Punting on quota semantics: we shouldn't change quota accounting now. For safety, hedged extra tokens should be charged to the originating provisional token until we have robust double-charge protection.
neil: Action items:
- neil: draft RFC by EOD Monday (admission->hedger contract + examples)
- jia: prototype header plumbing in router proxy (spike 2d)
- sam: add telemetry tags and dashboards (PR this week)
- amanda: coordinate canary + SRE runbook
- mike: run load test scenarios (cache miss heavy / bursty) and share results
ops-bot: reminder: create ticket INFRA-hedge-contract and link RFC.
lena: One more nuance: for Dedicated customers with pinned capacity we may want different defaults. Add tenant_tier to the header so hedger can use a tiered heuristic.
neil: Good catch. Include tenant_tier in RFC examples.
amanda: Sounds like a plan. If no objections I'll schedule a quick 30m sync post-RFC to align eng + SRE.
sam: :thumbsup:
jia: +1
mike: +1
neil: Thanks everyone, will start the RFC."
